then.text: Away and see the Cù-Sìth's glen on Skye, if you dare. Bring a jumper. Bring two.
Ice has just been freshly swept, and my team's been itching to skate on someone. Fancy a rematch?

else.text: Once a day, pal. The ice needs sweeping and I need a wee sit down. Tomorrow.
Another time, then. The offer stands.
The rink is cold in the way only a rink is cold: bright, clean and faintly smug. A woman in a woolly hat leans on a curling broom as if she were the Queen's own sweeper.
Mind the ice, it's freshly swept. Welcome to the rink. You've come a long way, and it's a cold way to finish.
I'm Isla. I keep the Frost Stone. I also keep the score, the kettle and the grudges. Mostly the kettle.
Frost creatures don't hurry. They just get there first. Sweep hard!
The Frost Stone, then. It doesn't make you colder. It makes you steadier, which in a bog is the same thing as dry.
Here, take these waders. Don't lose them. They've outlived two husbands and a ferry.
With the Frost Stone you can cross the deep bogs. We call it Bog-cross. The peat thinks twice, and you go over it in your waders, and the midges are, as ever, the only ones who suffer.
The old words say: Ceud mìle fàilte. A hundred thousand welcomes. Now away you go. Hurry hard.
Your phone buzzes. Professor Garside, who is plainly on a train and being told off by a conductor.
{player}! The Frost Stone! Nine! The hum's gone from a drone to a chord.
If the Enclosure's still on Loch Ness, they won't be for long. Skye is open now, and the Cairngorms. On Skye there's a glen with a dog in it.
Go carefully. The old stories say the Cù-Sìth barks three times and expects you to be indoors by the third. I don't know what happens after that. Nobody I've asked stayed to find out.
And the lady in Loch Ness is expecting you now, I'd say. Keep the waders on. Ask no one about the midges.
Back in town, the Wardens at the Skye and Cairngorms roads rolled up their tape, said they'd always meant to, and went to look at a stag.

rink_clubskip.text: Tuesday rink. The skip stands in the house and calls the shots, the rest sweep and try not to be told off. You, I'm afraid, are throwing.
The rings are the house, and the middle is the button. Your stone has to get past the far red line, the hog line, or it comes off. Closest to the button scores.
